market_holds: Sealed baseline (18:08 UTC): spot 48.86, event-implied move 12.67% (straddle 14.12%, ATM spread 52% of mid so indicative only), 25d skew -6.9 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.23 (call-heavy, consistent with takeover speculation), 20d run-up -27.2%, 5d -8.8%, 0.4% above the 52-week low, 47.8% below the high. Intraday at 14:20 ET AMBA was -14.7% against SOXX -7.2% and NXPI -4.9%. It slid from -10% to -15% through the afternoon while SOXX recovered from -10% to -7% (Yahoo 15m bars). From the 10-28 close to today AMBA fell 28.4% and SOXX 25.2% (Yahoo daily bars), so most of the run-in is the sector's AI-chip selloff, with an extra ~7 points today that I could not tie to any news. Consensus: Q3 (Oct) revenue $119.4M against a $115-124M guide, EPS ~$0.31-0.32, whisper $0.37, estimates flat over 60 days (Investing.com, 2026-11-24). Q4 (Jan) consensus $112.2M (Rosenblatt preview, which models $115M), roughly 'regular seasonality' off a ~$120M Q3, and FY27 +10-15% growth was conditioned on memory not hitting Q4. The past reactions are 6 of 7 prints down, median absolute move 16.8%, including beats; the 2026-09-03 print, which guided Q3 well above the Street, moved only -0.8%. M&A: FT (7-31) reported NXP talks; Qualcomm and Nvidia were reported as bidders in October; exclusive talks with NXP were reported 10-30; on 11-19 a Betaville alert said the deal was in final stages at $95-100/share with a fairness opinion under way. The stock gained 7.8% that day and gave it all back the next. A price at roughly half the rumoured deal price means the market assigns that deal very little probability.
view: This print turns on the Q4 (January-quarter) guide and on whatever management says, or declines to say, about a sale. On the guide: on the 09-03 call management said memory had little effect on Q2 and Q3, that Q4 visibility was weak, that they were 'talking to customers to make sure they can secure enough memory', and that 'the memory situation is dire for everybody'. Since then the memory market got worse. GoPro's 10-Q (an Ambarella customer) records 'unexpected price increases ranging from 70% to 80% in the last week of September 2026' and over 600% since Q4 2025, a 41% revenue drop and going-concern language. Team Group's CEO (11-02) called Q4 2026 to Q2 2027 the tightest stretch. Himax cut its Q4 guide 22-26% on an abrupt China auto order correction, Mobileye has roughly halved since September, and Arlo guided Q4 down ~5% sequentially with US channel weeks up from 5.9 to 14.9. Ambarella's own days of inventory are at 157 against 76 a year ago. Against that, the Street's Q4 number has not moved in 60 days, so the risk is a guide below $112M. There is a partial offset: enterprise security, Ambarella's stronger IoT half, is healthy (Hanwha Vision's security and AI camera revenue up 28.5% y/y in Q3 on price increases). So I lean toward a guide at or below consensus, and a stock that has fallen after 6 of the last 7 prints. The lean is weakened by three things. The stock has already been cut by 28% plus another 15% today into the print. It trades near 4x sales. And tomorrow's open depends heavily on a semiconductor tape that is moving 7-10% a day. Separately there is a real tail: a signed NXP deal announced with or around the release would roughly double the stock. I put that at about 7% inside the window, with a smaller chance that a release saying talks ended adds downside. Net, p_up is about 42, below 50 but not far enough for a bet.
unpriced: Sell-side Q4 estimates ($112.2M, flat for 60 days) do not visibly reflect the memory price spike after the last call (GoPro: +70-80% in the last week of September). The share price fell mostly with the sector, not on AMBA-specific estimate cuts, so a below-seasonal Q4 guide is not shown to be priced. Partly offset: the market also gives almost no value to a reported $95-100 deal.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism points down: memory costs and availability worsened after the 09-03 call, management had already said Q4 depended on customers securing memory, and the Q4 consensus has not moved. But the stock has already lost 28% in a month and 15% today, the sector tape alone moves it several points overnight, and a deal announcement is a fat right tail. My probability that the direction is right does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide at or above ~$112M with management saying customers have secured memory, or any announced agreement with NXP.

self_critique: The strongest case against: the stock has already fallen 28% in a month and 15% today into the print, sits at a 52-week low near 4x sales, and has a whisper above consensus. A Q3 beat with a merely in-line Q4 guide could produce a relief squeeze, and sentiment is already bearish. My memory evidence comes mostly from consumer camera makers (GoPro), which are now a small share of revenue, while enterprise security (Hanwha) is strong. The deal tail is real, and a confirmation of advanced talks or a signed deal would overwhelm everything else. The tape, with SOXX moving 7-10% a day, may decide tomorrow's open more than the release does. Taken together this keeps me from recommending and limits the lean to 42.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: it showed the 28% fall was mostly the sector, so the memory risk to the guide is not shown to be priced. P4 kept me from treating the drawdown as a cushion. The M&A tail does not fit the single-line framing well and needed its own probability.
